A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-function research. All pages, including v1 Appendices A–J and v2 Appendices A–O, are readable; corresponding methods, results, and figures can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1k and OpenWebText experiments, numerical ablations in Tables 3–6, and activation-fitting results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and ablations, plus CIFAR-10 training, decision-boundary comparisons, and transfer-learning results.

M1.justification: v2 replaces the Hermite and Fourier power-law initialization schemes with factorial-scaled series and new coefficient initializations. Fourier initial frequencies change from kπ/√3 to k, and Tropical outputs acquire a √2/n scaling. These procedural changes appear in Section 3 and Algorithms 1, 5, and 6. Tropical Rational activation and Hermite interpolation already existed in v1.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1k classification and OpenWebText language modeling are retained. v2 adds CIFAR-10 training, ImageNet-to-CIFAR-10 transfer learning, and noisy two-dimensional classification scenarios including moons and circles (Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.5; Appendices L, M, O). These substantially extend the evaluated data and task requirements.

E2.justification: SiLU becomes an evaluated GPT-2/OpenWebText baseline in Table 2 and Figures 14–15; previously it was only discussed or cited. The new CIFAR-10 comparison also includes ResNet50 with ReLU alongside ConvNeXt-T with GELU (Table 8). This is a limited comparator expansion, with GELU retained throughout.

E3.justification: v1 reports extremal benchmark scores, whereas v2 specifies reporting at fixed epochs or iterations. v2 also describes the main Fourier experiments as using the proposed initialization, replacing v1's GELU-fitting setting. New protocols include 300-epoch CIFAR-10 training and transfer learning with only the final linear layer and activation coefficients trainable. Unchanged ablation scores linked to revised initialization theorems do not establish that those ablations were rerun.

E4.justification: The four original degree, initialization, learnability, and clamping ablations retain their numerical results. v2 adds qualitative decision-boundary diagnostics across noisy datasets, a Tropical-Laurent quadratic-fitting illustration, and a brief factorial-versus-power-law stability comparison (Appendices M and H; Remark 3.15). These are limited supplementary extensions to the retained ablation evidence.

E5.justification: v1 mentions fixed seeds without specifying run counts or reporting uncertainty. v2 specifies three seeds, adds uncertainty to the main tables, and plots means with minimum-to-maximum shading. This establishes expanded reporting, not a known increase from a specified earlier run count. The uncertainty definition remains inconsistent: Sections 4.3–4.4 say standard deviation, while Tables 1–2 say standard error.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the earlier numerical summaries: Hermite ImageNet Top-1 changes from 82.34% to 82.18 ± 0.1270%, and GPT-2 validation perplexity from 18.39 to 18.80 ± 0.1905. Changed initialization and aggregation prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. v2 adds SiLU results, FLOP estimates, CIFAR-10 scores, decision-boundary findings, and fine-tuning curves. Tables 3–6 retain their scores, and v1 Figure 7 survives as v2 Figure 16.

T1.justification: The Hermite/Fourier moment calculations and initialization theorems are substantially revised around factorial series (Appendices C–D). v2 adds a Tropical initialization theorem and proof, a convex-conjugate definition, and a three-layer-collapse statement to the relocated polynomial-mapping proposition. The revision also introduces a mathematical inconsistency: Appendix D Eq. 67 omits the factor 1/2 implied by Eqs. 56 and 66.

C1.justification: The central contributions—variance-preserving initialization, learnable activation families, and polynomial mappings—remain. Performance claims are narrowed from outperforming traditional activations to successful training and matching or exceeding them. The abstract and conclusion now explicitly claim usefulness for fine-tuning, extending the previously proposed application with empirical support.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations connecting Tropical activations to convex conjugacy and decision-boundary geometry to polynomial, periodic, and max-plus structure. It qualifies Fourier/Tropical gains on CIFAR-10 as inconclusive. A dedicated limitations section reports 30–90% slower GPU training and claims inference-speed parity, while v1's explicit low-precision degree-three restriction is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix L/Table 7 adds a detailed CIFAR-10 recipe covering TIMM, four GPUs, batch size, AdamW, learning rate, scheduling, normalization, augmentation, and clipping. Appendix O specifies frozen and trainable parameters for transfer learning. Runtime information and implementation scaling are also revised. The torchortho code-and-weights availability claim is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Glorot and Bengio (2010), Gao et al. (2025), Krizhevsky et al. (2009), and Wightman (2019), while removing Hendrycks and Gimpel (2016) and Pandey and Phukan (2020). Attribution of variance-preserving initialization and the approximation-theory discussion are refined. The extensive positioning against earlier activation work and KANs otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes existing material: detailed moment derivations and the polynomial-mapping discussion move into appendices, while initialization theorems become the main methods narrative. The abstract is rewritten, the title shortened, the complexity discussion condensed into a separate section, and experiments reorganized around additional subsections and a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The MLP schematic moves to an appendix, and existing Hermite/Fourier fitting plots are merged into paired panels. Tables 1–2 replace initialization/learnability columns with computational-cost information and uncertainty displays. New configuration and results tables, decision-boundary panels, training curves, and fine-tuning plots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Replacing extrema-only reporting with fixed-checkpoint, three-seed summaries and visible run variation substantially strengthens the main empirical evidence. The transfer-learning experiment tests a previously proposed application, while explicit runtime costs and narrower performance claims improve assessment of practical value. These gains outweigh v2's conflicting SD/SE labels, unclear linkage between retained ablation scores and revised initializations, and the localized Fourier-proof factor error.
